notes: *** SHORTFALL AGAINST THE REQUEST, STATED UP FRONT *** The task asked for 4 Result=P vectors from SigVer.rsp [P-384,SHA-384]. That section does not contain 4: it contains exactly 3 Result=P and 12 Result=F. This is not an extraction bug -- every one of the 75 curve/SHA sections in SigVer.rsp has exactly the same 3 P / 12 F shape (file totals: 225 P, 900 F), because the file is built as 3 valid signatures plus 3 mutated variants of each of the four kinds '1 - Message changed', '2 - R changed', '3 - S changed', '4 - Q changed'. The FIPS 186-2 archive 186-2ecdsatestvectors.zip was downloaded and checked too and is also 3 P / 12 F per section. So 4 Result=P ECDSA vectors simply do not exist in any official CAVP SigVer.rsp. Instead of inventing a fourth, p384_sha384 holds the 3 that exist, and the extra 4th valid P-384/SHA-384 vector is supplied in the clearly separated p384_sha384_extra_valid array (see below). p521_sha512 does meet the request exactly: 3 Result=P, 2 Result=F.

*** SECOND DEVIATION FROM THE TASK TEXT: THE P-521 ECDH WIDTH. *** The task said 'P-521 coordinates are left-zero-padded to 66 bytes' in the vector file. That is true of SigVer.rsp, but NOT of KAS_ECC_CDH_PrimitiveTest.txt: measured over its whole [P-521] section, QCAVSx/QCAVSy/dIUT/QIUTx/QIUTy are all exactly 136 hex chars = 68 BYTES (two bytes wider than the 66-byte field), while ZIUT is 132 hex chars = 66 bytes. The [P-384] section is uniform at 96 hex chars = 48 bytes for every field. So for ecdh_p521 each value was stripped of leading zeros and re-padded to 132 hex chars; the numeric value is unchanged, only the byte-string form is normalised to the field width the task asked for. No value lost significant digits (asserted at build time).

Qx/Qy BYTE LENGTHS, MEASURED. Across the whole [P-384,SHA-384] section the raw Qx hex lengths are [96] and Qy [96] characters; across the whole [P-521,SHA-512] section Qx is [131] and Qy [131] characters. In the emitted records every qx/qy is therefore exactly 96 hex chars (48 bytes) for P-384 and exactly 132 hex chars (66 bytes) for P-521 -- asserted at build time. qx/qy are left-zero-padded to the full field width when CAVP stored them shorter.

R/S: r and s ARE VERBATIM, r_padded/s_padded ARE FIELD-WIDTH SAFE. The task fixed no width for r/s, so r and s are copied exactly as SigVer.rsp writes them (lowercase, no 0x, no separators). Measured raw hex lengths over the whole sections: [P-384,SHA-384] r [96] / s [96], [P-521,SHA-512] r [131] / s [131]. WATCH OUT: P-521 r/s are 131 characters -- an ODD number, because a P-521 scalar is < 2^521 and so needs at most 131 hex digits. Python's bytes.fromhex() and any fixed-width byte comparison will therefore fail on them, even though int(r, 16) is fine. Every record therefore also carries r_padded and s_padded, the same integers left-zero-padded to the full field width (96 hex chars / 48 bytes for P-384, 132 hex chars / 66 bytes for P-521), which are safe to bytes.fromhex() directly. r_padded/s_padded are additions, not replacements: r and s remain the untouched CAVP text.

Msg IS THE RAW MESSAGE, NOT A PRE-COMPUTED DIGEST. In SigVer.rsp the Msg field is the message to be hashed by the implementation with the SHA named in the section header. Measured Msg lengths: [P-384,SHA-384] [128] bytes, [P-521,SHA-512] [128] bytes (both 128 bytes, i.e. neither 48 nor 64, which rules out the digest interpretation). To verify a record: digest = SHA-384(msg_hex bytes) for p384_sha384, SHA-512(msg_hex bytes) for p521_sha512, then verify (r,s) against (qx,qy) on the named curve.

result_reason keeps CAVP's full Result text, including the failure annotation, e.g. 'F (2 - R changed)'; result is the bare verdict 'P' or 'F'. The task's schema only asked for the bare verdict, so result holds that and the annotation is preserved alongside it.

ECDH RECORD MAPPING (KAS_ECC_CDH_PrimitiveTest.txt). Each CAVP block is COUNT/QCAVSx/QCAVSy/dIUT/QIUTx/QIUTy/ZIUT. Mapped as: peer_x=QCAVSx, peer_y=QCAVSy (the peer's public point), priv=dIUT (the IUT's private scalar) and shared=ZIUT (the x-coordinate of dIUT*QCAVS). QIUTx/QIUTy (the IUT's own public point) are not part of the requested schema and are intentionally omitted. ecdh_p384 uses [P-384] COUNT=0 and COUNT=1 (header at line 615, COUNT lines 617 and 625); ecdh_p521 uses [P-521] COUNT=0 and COUNT=1 (header at line 818, COUNT lines 820 and 828). peer_x/peer_y/shared are emitted at the true field width, 48 bytes (96 hex chars) for P-384 and 66 bytes (132 hex chars) for P-521; the raw ZIUT hex lengths in the source were [96, 96] (P-384) and [132, 132] (P-521).

CROSS-CHECK PERFORMED. Every record in this file was re-verified against OpenSSL 3.2.1 by work/verify_vectors.py, which rebuilds the P-384/P-521 public key from qx/qy and the signature from r/s and runs `openssl dgst -sha384/-sha512 -verify`, and rebuilds the ECDH keys to run `openssl pkeyutl -derive`. Result: every Result=P record including p384_sha384_extra_valid reports 'Verified OK', every Result=F record reports 'Verification Failure', and every ECDH derive reproduces shared byte for byte.
